claim: Defects in WRN and WRNIP1 ATPase activities cause a diversity of nucleotide (nt) misincorporations opposite DNA lesions by Y-family Pols.

claim: WRN and WRNIP1 ATPases restrain nt misincorporations by tightening the active site of the TLS Pol.

claim: The combined actions of WRN and WRNIP1 ATPases in preventing nt misincorporations and of WRN exonuclease in removing misinserted nts confer an enormous rise in the fidelity of Y-family Pols.

claim: The role of WRN ATPase activity gets modified by the components of the Y-family Pol multiprotein ensemble to impact the active site of the TLS Pol, limiting misincorporations.
source: Hence, we suggest that rather than employing the WRN ATPase activity for unwinding the DNA helix, the role of this activity gets modified by the components of the Y-family Pol multiprotein ensemble – that include WRN, WRNIP1, Rev1, and likely other proteins – to impact the active site of the TLS Pol, limiting misincorporations.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation proposed in the Discussion section based on the observed data.

claim: WRN and WRNIP1 ATPase activities play an unprecedented role in imposing high fidelity on TLS by Y-family Pols.

evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion section and supported by mutation frequency and mutational spectra data throughout the manuscript.

claim: For error-free TLS through CPDs by Polη, all three activities (WRN ATPase, WRNIP1 ATPase, and WRN exonuclease) make a prominent contribution – the WRN and WRNIP1 ATPases by restraining nt misincorporations and the WRN exonuclease by expunging nts misincorporated by Polη.

claim: The combined action of WRN and WRNIP1 ATPases along with WRN 3' to 5' exonuclease provides a safeguard against genomic instability and tumorigenesis.
source: Our evidence that the combined action of WRN and WRNIP1 ATPases along with WRN 3' to 5' exonuclease confers an enormous rise in the fidelity of TLS by Y-family Pols identifies the means by which these otherwise highly error-prone TLS Pols have been adapted to function in an error-free manner; thereby, providing a safeguard against genomic instability and tumorigenesis, as opposed to the deeply set percept that they contribute to it.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion section and supported by mutation frequency data throughout the manuscript.
